problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & -2 \\ -12 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2k \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.worked_solution:
We need to solve the equation $Ax=0.$ First, we find the row echelon form of $A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

The second equation tells us that ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that $x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is the only solution to this system.

Therefore, $\text{Null}(A)={0}.$
